subject: SLA safety margin & monthly credit pool proposal
messages:
From: EdgeWave Procurement <procurement@edgewave.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@riverside.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Service commitments: request for monthly credit pool and uptime buffer

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we prepare the purchase order we need to square on two items in your standard SLA before procurement can sign:

1) Monthly credit pool vs per-incident credits — we'd prefer a single monthly pool (to be drawn down as incidents occur) with a hard cap so our finance team can model exposure.
2) Safety margin / maintenance carveout — EdgeWave runs large nightly batch jobs and occasional planned capacity maintenance. We need a defined "safety margin" that excludes short scheduled maintenance and also a latency-tail SLO carveout for batched inference spikes.

Attached are our suggested redlines (EdgeWave_SLA_Redlines_v3.pdf) and a sample monthly-credit-pool calculation. High level asks: baseline uptime of 99.95% for production endpoints, a monthly pool equal to 25% of one-month service fee capped at 3x average daily spend, and a 2-hour rolling maintenance window that doesn't trigger credits.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is open to a monthly-pool structure and the proposed maintenance carveout? If needed we can schedule a quick call tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet.

Best,
Procurement Team
EdgeWave

---
Attachments: EdgeWave_SLA_Redlines_v3.pdf (pdf, 145KB)
Attachments: monthly-credit-pool.xlsx (xls, 24KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: EdgeWave Procurement <procurement@edgewave.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@riverside.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service commitments: request for monthly credit pool and uptime buffer

Samir / EdgeWave procurement team — thanks for the clear redlines and the spreadsheet. Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (product/ops) so we can respond to the specific asks.

Quick responses up front:
- Monthly credit pool: we can offer a monthly pool model for certain commitment tiers. We'll need to align on the cap mechanics (percent of monthly fee vs fixed multiple).
- Maintenance carveouts: we generally allow scheduled maintenance windows and small maintenance gracebands, but the 2-hour rolling carveout needs tighter definition (frequency, notification lead time, and whether it applies per-region or globally).
- Latency tail carveout for batch spikes: this is a reasonable ask for batched inference customers; we typically treat tail-latency events differently for batch workloads vs interactive routing. We'll propose a separate latency-trigger definition and monitoring thresholds.

Next steps: Laura / Ben / Monica — please see the attached redlines from EdgeWave and the spreadsheet. Can Laura provide a legal counter on pool/cap language? Ben, can you propose operational limits (frequency, max hours/month) for the maintenance carveout and a latency-tail definition we can stand behind?

Samir — happy to do a 30-minute call to walk numbers. I'm available Tue-Wed morning PT.

Thanks,
Marcus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments referenced: EdgeWave_SLA_Redlines_v3.pdf, monthly-credit-pool.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, EdgeWave Procurement <procurement@edgewave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service commitments: request for monthly credit pool and uptime buffer

Marcus / Samir / team — thanks for the heads-up. I reviewed the redlines and the proposal; below are our suggested counterpoints written to balance operational risk with commercial certainty.

1) Baseline uptime: Our standard production commitment is 99.9% in the hosted tier. For large reserved commitments (which EdgeWave is targeting) we can elevate to 99.95% with a minimum 12‑month committed spend. If EdgeWave requires 99.95% without a revenue commitment, we need to discuss higher remedy caps.

2) Monthly pool mechanics: We can support a monthly-pool remedy instead of per-incident credits. Our recommended language: monthly pool equals X% of monthly recurring fees (we propose 15%), with an absolute cap equal to 2x the average daily spend multiplied by 30. The pool is drawn down in chronological order and resets at the start of each billing month. We cannot accept an open-ended multiple (e.g., 3x) without a corresponding insurance-style standby fee.

3) Scheduled maintenance & safety margin: We will permit up to 6 scheduled maintenance windows per quarter (each up to 2 hours) that are excluded from uptime calculations provided EdgeWave receives at least 72 hours' notice and windows are executed during the mutually agreed maintenance window (00:00–06:00 regional local time). Unplanned maintenance and emergency mitigations will be evaluated case-by-case and may not be excluded.

4) Latency-tail carveout for batched workloads: Product/ops team to propose a measurable definition. Ben — see below.

Ben / Monica — operational asks: please draft a short appendix that defines: a) batch vs interactive endpoints, b) latency SLOs and tail thresholds (p99.5/p99.9), c) acceptable burst profile (e.g., sustained >N tokens/sec for >M minutes), and d) auto-fallback behavior that triggers when tail breaches occur. EdgeWave needs the appendix to be auditable for their procurement.

I'll prepare a contract-side counter with the above language and pass it to Samir's procurement team tomorrow.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

---
Quoted: "Attached are our suggested redlines... High level asks: baseline uptime of 99.95%..."

From: Samir Patel <samir.p@riverside.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeWave Procurement <procurement@edgewave.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service commitments: request for monthly credit pool and uptime buffer

Laura / Marcus — thanks for the thorough counter. The structure you proposed (monthly pool, capped multiple, defined maintenance windows with 72h notice) is workable. A few clarifying items before we proceed to DocuSign:

- EdgeWave is happy to move baseline to 99.95% provided we sign a 12-month commitment at the tier discussed (see HubSpot deal referenced).
- For the monthly pool cap, we can accept 2x average daily spend * 30 as the cap instead of our original 3x request.
- Regarding scheduled maintenance: 72 hours' notice is acceptable if Redwood commits to perform no more than 4 such windows per quarter for EdgeWave's production region for the first 12 months.
- For the latency appendix: Ben — can you draft the appendix with p99.5 and p99.9 thresholds and the burst profile language by end of next week? EdgeWave needs that for internal audit.

If those items are confirmed I'll ask procurement to expect a final counter and a DocuSign packet. Appreciate the flexibility.

Best,
Samir Patel
Head of Cloud Operations, EdgeWave

---
Next steps: internal — Laura will prepare the legal counter (contract language); Ben will draft the latency appendix; Marcus to schedule sign-off call with EdgeWave procurement the week of Mar 1.
